# Grounding AI in Truth {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

When you control the context, you control the answer

## The "Context First" Rule {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="workflow" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em;"}
The wrong way: Open AI → type a question → hope for the best.
:::

. . .

::: {data-id="workflow" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em; margin-top: 0.8em;"}
The right way: **Upload source → instruct → grounded result.**
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-important}
## The rule
No upload = no trust. **Context comes before content.**
:::

## The Trust Layer {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="trust" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
Hallucinations happen when AI **doesn't know** the answer but **tries to please you**
by guessing.
:::

. . .

The **Trust Layer** forces the AI to answer from *your sources* as its only truth —
*"Based **only** on this document, summarize… and cite every point."*

## The Golden Rule {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.3em;"}
**If it doesn't have a citation, it didn't happen.**
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.8em;"}
Demand page references. Then click them and check the source text.
:::
